request.rationale: The prior characterization artifact was invalidated by array aliasing. request.description: Re-run the full compiled-dynamics characterization after verified snapshot isolation.
request.rationale: M4 established that the repaired production path preserves independent repeated transitions and the required diagnostic coverage. This rerun supplies the first scientifically interpretable candidate-free evidence for actuation authority, branch feasibility, and sampled hold timing; the earlier aliased M3 artifact is not used as evidence.

request.candidates_and_roles: No candidate exists. Working, best-known, and retained roles are empty. M3's completed artifact is retained only as execution history with its aliasing limitation and is not used as scientific evidence; M5 is the current physical characterization, not a learned candidate.
request.cumulative_resource_use: Completed candidate-free measurements M1, M3, M4 and M5; M2 had one implementation failure and was reaccepted after repair. No training steps, inquiry allocation, candidate role assignment, or official assessment were used. The campaign laboratory now contains the reusable compiled-dynamics characterization and its defect-sensitive check.
request.current_goal_gap: No learned candidate or development success evidence exists, so the gap to 98% is currently unmeasured. The remaining scientific gap is to determine whether a policy exposed to the official full radius distribution can reach and maintain the 1 cm sampled hold, and whether failures are concentrated in omitted inner-radius/branch regimes or in generic braking and stabilization.
request.current_synthesis: Observed evidence: M1 compatibility verification passed for the new candidate-free MuJoCo characterization path, and M4 independently passed the repaired behavioral checks with six deterministic resets, 36 synchronized transitions, both IK branch summaries, and ten internal substeps. These are implementation-validity evidence, not policy-performance evidence. M3 completed after an initial serialization repair but its artifact is not used scientifically because inspection found NumPy view aliasing: distinct trajectory rows were not preserved. M5 is the repaired characterization and is the first interpretable physical evidence. It compiled the official XML at 0.002 s with frame_skip 10 (0.020 s policy interval), zero gravity, two joints and two actuators. Compiled bodies have finite masses and inertias; the actuator summaries show control limits [-1,1], gain 1, gear 5, no force limit, and controlled saturated input produced +/-5 actuator torque. From zero state, five 20 ms saturated shoulder updates reached qvel about 9.81 rad/s; changing to the opposing saturated command changed qvel from about 9.81 to -1.05 rad/s in one further control interval and produced about -400 rad/s^2 acceleration. This supports a consequential braking/timing and stabilization mechanism, not an initial claim of insufficient authority. The repaired trace also confirms the compiled zero-pose end effector is [0.22, 0, 0.02]. A deterministic substep trace changed distance by about 6.70 mm within one 20 ms action, while the official endpoint samples only the final distance; all ten substeps in that controlled trace were outside the 1 cm band. This demonstrates that endpoint statistics do not establish continuous-time stability, but it does not establish policy failure. On a 29-by-360 official radius/bearing grid, each named open and folded IK branch had 9860/10440 (94.44%) samples within compiled joint limits; among legal samples the Jacobian condition number ranged up to about 5.29 and the minimum singular value was at least about 0.0415. This makes branch and limit effects consequential, but the artifact does not compute the union of feasible branches, so it cannot establish that 5.56% of targets are infeasible. Competing explanations remain: (1) the baseline exposure omits radii below 0.14 m and may cause an inner-radius coverage/branch failure; (2) high actuation authority and sampled braking transients may cause generic hold interruptions; (3) exact branch-union feasibility or bearing concentration may impose a geometry-related ceiling; and (4) observation/runtime realization may still matter. Current evidence favors first measuring a complete learned candidate under official geometry with hold-interruption and radius/branch diagnostics, not altering physics or assuming reach-only reward is adequate. The evidence does not establish a training-method effect or any official success rate.
request.decision_frontier: The unresolved decision is whether the first learning direction should prioritize distribution coverage, stabilization/control timing, or a geometry/branch intervention. Discriminating evidence is a complete candidate comparison or mechanism-linked evaluation under the official radius range: success, maximum consecutive hold, interruptions, first reach, final/minimum distance, action saturation, velocity, and target-radius/bearing strata, with runtime/normalization context. If an outer-only candidate reaches reliably above 0.14 m but fails below it while hold behavior is otherwise intact, full-radius exposure becomes the leading route. If failures span radii and show low minimum distance followed by short holds, braking/stabilization becomes the leading route. If failures align with the presently sampled limit-infeasible branch subsets, compute branch-union feasibility and reconsider whether a geometry/branch-aware policy representation is needed. If matched transitions or runtime inspection reveal inconsistency, memory/normalization or system-identification work becomes consequential. The current characterization did not measure any candidate, did not compute branch-union feasibility, and did not observe continuous behavior between recorded 2 ms substeps; those limits remain explicit.
request.human_goal_connection: The human goal is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes, where each success requires an uninterrupted 2 s position hold. The completed startup work establishes the physical and diagnostic basis for choosing the first learned-policy direction; it does not assess or certify goal progress.
request.next_direction_or_closure: Checkpoint startup and enter goal review. The next credible direction is to open the proposed bounded candidate/mechanism inquiry rather than request official assessment: train or restore a documented baseline as needed, measure it under official geometry, and compare it with a full-radius exposure while preserving hold-interruption diagnostics. This follows because M5 rules out treating omitted compiled authority as the first intervention, but leaves the coverage-versus-stabilization distinction unresolved and no policy has yet been assessed.
request.next_question: At goal review, should the campaign open a bounded inquiry comparing an outer-only baseline exposure with official full-radius exposure, using complete uninterrupted-hold and radius/branch diagnostics to determine whether the 98% route is primarily coverage or stabilization?
